rationale: The INDICATOR→SIGN swap is a substantive repair rather than cosmetics — it converts a degenerate one-sided gate (which produced no computable long-short stats) into a two-sided spread that actively shorts cheap-but-accelerating firms — though it remains a close descendant of the archived gen-0 signal and its short leg is deep-value stocks, which may fight the FF5 value factor.

This is a conjunctive value × asset-growth double sort, i.e. essentially the classic B/M and asset-growth anomalies combined, and the claim that MIN "cannot be replicated by any linear mix of HML and CMA loadings" confuses a nonlinear construction rule with factor exposure — the resulting portfolio will load heavily on both HML and CMA regardless.

With dvc typically an order of magnitude smaller than capx for most firms, this ratio is dominated by −(capx+aqc)/market cap, making it a near-rediscovery of the capital-investment-to-price anomaly dressed as a payout measure, and the "not a free-cash-flow yield" defense concedes it omits the one term (operating cash flow) that would make the allocation story economically well-posed.

Incremental EBITDA per dollar of lagged capex is a genuinely different construct from investment level or growth — it is a marginal-productivity measure rather than a quantity — the sign logic and the winsorized small-denominator handling are internally consistent, and the value leg's role as a conditioner is economically coherent rather than a repackaged quality-times-value composite.

The economic mechanism is the same rich-valuation-plus-empire-building story as the archived Expensive_Externally_Funded_Empire (which already delivered strong FMB but a weak, wrong-signed portfolio spread), and the proposal swaps both legs without diagnosing why that FMB/alpha divergence occurred; separately, COALESCE(gdwl,0) inside DELTA will manufacture spurious first-time-reporting jumps.

Replacing the investment level with capex acceleration is a defensible refinement that shifts the signal from chronically capital-intensive firms to the turn in spending, and the diagnosis of which gen-0 signal was sign-consistent is accurate, but a second difference of an annual ratio is noisy and will cost coverage, so the gain over the parent signal is uncertain.
